diagnosis.statement: The apparent single Pineau–Vicol local criterion contains two distinct consumer interfaces. The generator-to-enstrophy step uses annular pressure quantitatively as written, while the downstream one-slice enstrophy criterion explicitly admits suitability instead. This removes one gluing obstacle only after switching consumers.

local_mathematical_failure.statement: Finite I controls the time-averaged critical dissipation ledger and yields a late good-time scaled-enstrophy upper bound of order I, but no source-valid mechanism contracts that bound to the fixed PV epsilon threshold when I is arbitrary.

local_to_global_or_interface_failure.statement: The generic AB finite-I producer does not supply the pointwise local Type-I hypothesis of PV_E/PV_G. Passing through AB local compactness also loses the pressure/generator time-slice strength required by PV_G.

process_failure.statement: A useful pressure-removability observation was noticed before a valid v3 PreActionFibreReceipt existed. Under current RAKL pre_action_receipt semantics the episode is RETROSPECTIVE_ONLY and cannot earn prospective gate credit.

obstruction.statement: To consume PV_E without stronger pressure hypotheses, the lane must first be inside the pointwise local Type-I suitable-weak subclass and then force one late scaled-enstrophy dip below θ_*²/4. Compactness or finite I alone does neither.

lesson.statement: When a regularity proof factors as generator→enstrophy→epsilon-regularity, audit the internal consumer boundary: suitability may discharge pressure at the enstrophy stage even if pressure remains load-bearing in the generator stage.

motif.scope: same-equation local regularity interfaces; proposal/shadow only
motif.statement: Switch to the nearest downstream consumer whose hypotheses match the producer before trying to strengthen a nonlocal pressure interface.

nonclaims: no theorem that finite I cannot imply the missing trigger by a different Navier–Stokes argument
same-context expert review is 0/3 independent review credit
